status.title: Status
status.no_zones_description: Add a DNS zone to let other modules create and change its records.
status.audit_log_description: Every change to records and every call by another module is logged. Open the system logs, filtered on dnshelper audit.

action.list-provider-zones: List the zones of the DNS host

zones.title: Zones
zones.intro: A zone is a domain whose DNS records other modules may create and change, through your DNS host's API. Each zone uses a credential (an API token) for its DNS host.
zones.no_zones_description: Add a zone to get started.
zones.change_credential_help: Pick the credential the zone should use from now on. Records are not touched.
zones.remove_zone_description: Stop managing {zone}. Modules will no longer be able to change its records.
zones.remove_zone_explanation: The records at your DNS host are not deleted, and the credential is kept.

credentials.title: Credentials
credentials.intro: Credentials are API tokens for your DNS host. One credential can serve several zones, and rotating a token is a single edit. Secrets are never shown again after saving: leave a secret field empty to keep it. Prefer tokens limited to the zones you need.
credentials.no_credentials_description: A credential is created together with the first zone that uses it.
credentials.remove_description: Delete the credential {name}. The token stays valid at your DNS host: revoke it there if it should no longer work.
credentials.secret_help: Leave empty to keep the stored value

wizard.title: Add zone
wizard.provider_intro: Choose where the zone is hosted.
wizard.least_privilege: Create an API token that can only edit the zones you add here, not your whole account. The token is stored on this node and included in backups.
wizard.credential_name_help: A label for this credential, to recognise it later
wizard.zone_intro_listed: Choose one of the zones this credential can manage, or type its name.
wizard.zone_intro_typed: Type the name of the zone. This DNS host cannot list its zones.
wizard.find_zones: Find zones used by my modules
wizard.cannot_discover: Cannot look at the other modules
wizard.suggestions_help: Domains used by your mail, web server and other modules. Select one to use it.
wizard.validated_list-zones: The credential can see the zone at the DNS host.
wizard.validated_get-records: The credential can read the zone's records.
wizard.read_only: This DNS host cannot replace records through its API, so some changes by other modules may fail.
wizard.write_test_help: Optionally create and delete a temporary TXT record to prove that changes are allowed. Nothing else is touched.

access.title: Access
access.intro: Other modules change DNS records by calling dnshelper. A module can only do what a rule below allows: without a rule it is refused everything, even if it may call dnshelper. Administrators are not restricted by these rules.
access.roles_help: For a module to be allowed to call dnshelper at all, its image must declare this authorization (module developers set it in build-images.sh):
access.no_rules_description: No module can change records yet.
access.caller_placeholder: Choose a module or type a pattern
access.caller_help: module/mail1, or a pattern such as module/mail*
access.names_help: Separated by commas, relative to the zone: @ is the zone itself, * matches anything, for example *._domainkey. Use * for all names.
access.types_help: Separated by commas, for example TXT, MX. Use * for all types (needed to delete without giving a type).
access.invalid_caller: Use module/ followed by the module id, like module/mail1
access.invalid_names: Use letters, digits, @, _, ., - and the wildcards * and ?
access.invalid_types: Use record types like TXT, or *
access.remove_description: Delete this rule for {caller}. The module will lose this access at once.

dns_error.not_permitted: Not allowed by the access rules
dns_error.zone_not_found: Zone not found at the DNS host, or not managed here
dns_error.auth_failed: The DNS host rejected the credential, or it has no access to this zone
dns_error.unsupported: This DNS host does not support that
dns_error.conflict: That would leave the zone invalid
dns_error.credential_in_use: The credential is still used by a zone
